picks.title: How (and why) to build agent-first apps
picks.excerpt: Builder.io's Steve Sewell lays out an 'agent-native' design pattern where anything the UI can do, an agent can do too -- unifying human and agent actions through a shared action abstraction. A forward-looking take on how product/UX design must change when AI agents become first-class users of the interface.
picks.rationale: Concrete design pattern (shared action abstraction) that changes how designers scope UI when agents are first-class users; distinct how-to follow-up published 5 days after the earlier agent-native piece.

picks.title: Game AI Expert Explains Where AI Actually Belongs in Game Development—And The Risks
picks.excerpt: AI researcher Luke Dicken (ex-Zynga innovation lead, former Head of AI at Take-Two) argues generative AI's real value is enabling adaptive, player-facing experiences rather than automating existing content pipelines, and that studios should invest in R&D that amplifies creative talent instead of replacing it. A creative-tooling perspective on where AI helps craft versus where it just adds risk.
picks.rationale: A senior practitioner's framing of where AI amplifies creative craft vs. where it only adds risk — useful judgment for designers deciding where to adopt gen-AI in a pipeline.

picks.title: Nexthena 1.2.1 released
picks.excerpt: Release notes for Nexthena 1.2.1, an AI-assisted infinite-canvas whiteboard/design tool, adding new workflow and localization updates. A small but concrete example of AI moving into the everyday visual-collaboration and diagramming layer of a designer's toolkit.
picks.rationale: A concrete, shippable AI-assisted whiteboard release — novel tool news at the everyday visual-collaboration layer, from a distinct outlet and category.
